label: first step of the sequence (t = 0)
explanation: Sequence-start feature: fires on step t = 0 of every sequence (100% rate) and essentially nowhere else (1 stray activation out of ~6.5M other dev steps, in the copy phase). Activation is nearly constant (mean 2.216, median 2.222, max 2.235) regardless of which token is input, L, or anything else; rate is uniform across first tokens. It does not fire on later original-phase steps, the <DEL> delimiter, or copy steps. Its share of activations varies with L only because longer sequences have more non-t0 steps.

issues: No real problems found. On the test split, the predicate t == 0 scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0, correlation 0.99998, and finds 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

Dev profile matches the explanation: 500000/500000 t=0 steps fire. The single stray activation is at t=4 in the copy phase (recall_idx=1, which means L=3). Nothing fires on the delimiter. Magnitude: mean 2.216, median 2.222, max 2.235.
The per-L rate drop is just the denominator effect, as the explanation says: each L gets about 1/6 of the activation mass, in proportion to how many sequences have that L.
